This is a sad little story, with a happy ending. Apologies as I am not great at story telling, but here goes:

A couple of months ago, my beloved companion of 16 years, Chino passed away. She had been listless and 'spaced out' so I took her to the vet, who did some tests and came back with the news: Massive kidney failure. She was suffering terribly and the kindest course of action was to have her put to sleep. Now, I am a stoic, tough guy, but I was in tears in the exam room, holding my sweet, gentle little lady as the vet administered the injection. I had never known a cat so friendly and tolerant. So loving. I was devastated.

A week or so later, I arrived at the vet to collect her ashes, which I was going to scatter under her favourite bush in the garden. On my way out I noticed a poster on the wall. It was for a rescue cat. Now, I was feeling the absence of a cat in the house very acutely, as any cat owner will tell you: they have big souls. This cat was 16 months, so unlikely to be adopted as everyone wants a kitten. I felt an immediate pang of compassion.

So, with Chino mourned for and laid to rest, I made an enquiry to the animal welfare dept. and the council lady told me this particular cat's story: Her owner had done a runner from the flat they lived in, leaving the poor cat locked in without food or water for 4 weeks. When bailiffs entered the property, they found her near death, only alive because she had been living on dirty dish water and toilet water. That is when they contacted animal welfare. I cannot abide cruelty or neglect of animals and upon hearing this, I knew instantly what I had to do.

As my previous cats have been pretty long lived and I was well known to the vet, I skipped all the paperwork and they arranged for me to take her home that Friday after the vets had checked her out and given her the usual shots. She did the usual 'hide under the sofa in terror' routine cats always do in a new house. However, she soon ventured out and started exploring. Now, every night she snuggles up to me on my bed and stays until morning, when I need to be woken at 5:30 for breakfast. Then it is a packed day of climbing trees in the garden and racing around the house, jumping out on her unsuspecting owner as he climbs the stairs.

I think it is safe to say she is very, very happy here....

In 2014 an organization called Polska Biega started an internet questionaire to find out more about runners. 60 000 runners took part and here are some of the stats:

  • 61% were men, 39% women
  • 21% aged 15-24, 38% 25-34, 29% 35-44, 12% 45+
  • 94% said they run for health, 2/3 said running has changed the way they eat.
  • Runners value quality, 80% said they are willing to pay more for quality items,
  • 60% like trying new items/ gadgets
  • 80% call running an addiction and 1/3 share their addition on social media
  • 60% use running to combat stress
  • 30% get up early in the morning to run
  • 28% have been running shorter than one year, 17% one year, 19% two years, 16% 3-4 years, 20% 5+ years (more women are entering the sport with 36% running shorter than one year compaired to 23% men)
  • 23% run 4+ times a week, 59% run 2-3 times a week, 11% once a week, rest less than once a week
  • 20% do 10km a week, 33% do 10-20km a week, 31% do 20-40km a week, 13% 40+km per week (More women in the 10km a week range, 30% compared to 18% men) (More men in the 40+km a week range, 17% compared to 7% women)
  • 52% continue running in the winter (Polish winter)
  • 17% have organized training sesions
  • 85% often run alone, 60% sometimes run with another person, 30% sometimes run in a larger group, 15% sometimes run with an animal
  • 85% often run on pavement, 73% often run trail, 8% often use treadmill
  • 60% consider running their main sport, other popular activities among runners: cycling, swimming, aerobic, hiking, team sports, winter sports, gym, tenis
  • 58% said they have taken part in an organized event, 31% 5k, 79% 5-10k, 46% half marathon, 26% marathon, 4% ultra
  • 47% have one pair of running shoes, 31% have 2, 10% have 3, 5% have 4+
  • 70% use running apps, 70% listen to music
  • 12% of women identified as vegetarian, 5% of men

Lots and lots of other stats and commentary in the full 95 page report. In Polish of course. http://polskabiega.sport.pl/pdf/nsb_raport.pdf
